article_sentences: US Vice President JD Vance has said that President Donald Trump was sending a message to Iran when he posted an AI-generated video that appeared to show the US military blowing up oil facilities on Iran's Kharg Island earlier on Monday.
"The president likes to switch it up on social media a little bit," Vance said when asked about Trump's post at a press conference.
"He would be the first to say he doesn't make announcements about military actions on social media, but I think that he's sending a message to the Iranians," he added.
Earlier on Monday, Hamid Bovard, the chief executive of the National Iranian Oil Company, denied that the US had destroyed oil facilities on Kharg.

stories.title: Jordan intelligence chief spearheaded move to arrest US journalist Ali Younes
stories.summary: Jordan intelligence chief spearheaded move to arrest US journalist Ali Younes Submitted by Elis Gjevori on Mon, 08/31/2026 - 14:58 Jordan faces calls to lose billions in US funding unless it releases American journalist its holding for allegedly reposting an article Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin meets with General Ahmad Husni, Director of the General Intelligence Directorate of Jordan, at Department of Homeland Security headquarters in Washington 15 April (DHS photo by Mikaela McGee) Off Major General Ahmad Husni, the director of Jordan’s General Intelligence Department, spearheaded the arrest of prominent American-Jordanian investigative journalist Ali Younes, Middle East
article_sentences: Major General Ahmad Husni, the director of Jordan’s General Intelligence Department, spearheaded the arrest of prominent American-Jordanian investigative journalist Ali Younes, Middle East Eye has learned.
A source close to the investigation said that the intelligence official had signed off on the move to arrest Younes, who has worked for Al Jazeera and Dropsite, amongst others.

Seperately, Ammon News, a media outlet reportedly close to Jordan’s intelligence services, published an article on Younes’s arrest last week that revealed further details about the state’s campaign against him.
The article linked his arrest to his alleged “attacks on the Jordanian Armed Forces” and efforts to “disseminate misleading information originating from a Jewish source (Aaron Magid)”.
Jordanian intelligence officers detained Younes on 17 August after he arrived at Queen Alia International Airport.
They questioned him before ordering him to appear before prosecutors in Amman.
The charges levelled against Younes are highly unusual.
Security officials have centred their case on his alleged reposting of an article by Aaron Magid, published in The American Conservative, questioning US aid to Jordan.
Jordan has received $33.8bn in American assistance over the past 75 years and is set to receive billions more under continuing agreements with Washington.
“Magid used Younes as a tool to undermine national security and Jordan's positive stances on Arab and Islamic issues,” the Ammon News article said.
Younes is correspondent for the US-based investigative outlet Drop Site News who previously worked for Al Jazeera and has contributed to The New York Times, Fox News, CNN and the BBC.
The media campaign against Younes in Jordan has also raised fears for his safety amid online death threats and intimidation.

stories.title: Cooperation between Russia and India constantly reaches new frontiers — Modi
stories.summary: The Indian prime minister stressed that moving forward together had been the shared vision
article_sentences: NEW DELHI, August 31.

Russian·Indian cooperation is constantly reaching new heights, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said at a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Bishkek.

"We are extremely pleased that our cooperation is constantly reaching new frontiers and that we are working together for the benefit of the peoples of our countries," he said, according to a statement on X.
"Moving forward together has been our shared vision and will remain our guiding principle."

stories.title: What the SDF’s dissolution means for Syria’s Kurds and neighbouring Turkey
stories.summary: Nearly a week after the Syrian Democratic Forces agreed to dissolve, the consequences are beginning to take shape for Syria's Kurds and neighbouring Turkey. As the former US-backed force is absorbed into the Syrian state, questions remain over what the country's Kurds have secured in return – from language and political rights to protections for women – and what the end of more than a decade of Kurdish-led autonomy means for Turkey's own conflict with Kurdish militants.
